evals.prompt: I write a weekly newsletter about UX design for product teams. I have 800 subscribers. I want to grow faster. Should I be on TikTok? My posts there would be like '5 UX mistakes' type content.
evals.expected_output: The skill should evaluate TikTok against the persona and channel fit, not just give a generic 'yes, all channels are worth trying' answer. UX designers at product companies are professional, B2B audience — more likely LinkedIn or YouTube than TikTok. Should recommend evaluating where the persona actually spends time, likely push toward LinkedIn as higher-value for this audience, and recommend newsletter cross-promotions as the most direct growth tactic at 800 subscribers. Should not flat-out refuse TikTok but should give a realistic read on fit.
expectations: Evaluates TikTok against the B2B professional persona, not just as a general growth channel
Recommends LinkedIn or YouTube as higher-fit alternatives for a UX/product audience
Mentions newsletter cross-promotions or Sparkloop as a high-ROI tactic at 800 subscribers
Does not give a blanket 'yes, TikTok is worth it' without assessing audience fit
Emphasizes owned channel growth (email list) as the primary objective

evals.prompt: We publish 8 blog posts per month. We tweet links to each one. Nobody clicks. We also share on LinkedIn and get almost no engagement there either. What are we doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: The skill should diagnose the root problem: link-only posts on social platforms are not promotion — they're ads that nobody asked to see. Should explain platform-native content requirements (LinkedIn suppresses external links, Twitter threads outperform link tweets, etc.). Should recommend repurposing key insights as platform-native posts with the link as secondary. Should also question whether 8 blog posts per month is sustainable and whether the content itself is worth sharing.
expectations: Identifies link-only posting as the root problem, not posting frequency or platform choice
Explains platform-native content requirement (LinkedIn and Twitter both suppress raw link posts)
Recommends converting blog insights into platform-native formats (threads, carousels, etc.)
Does not recommend posting more frequently as the primary solution
Questions whether the content quality warrants sharing before assuming the problem is pure distribution

evals.prompt: I have a podcast for independent financial advisors. 650 downloads per episode. I want to double that in 12 months. My current promotion: I post the episode link on LinkedIn once, and once on Twitter. That's it. Build me a real promotion strategy.
evals.expected_output: A full promotion strategy for a B2B podcast. Should identify LinkedIn as the primary rented channel (financial advisors are on LinkedIn), recommend native audio clips or text excerpts as LinkedIn posts, recommend show notes as SEO-optimized blog posts, recommend guest appearances on other financial advisor podcasts, suggest newsletter cross-promotions if there's a corresponding newsletter, and build a post-publish promotion checklist. Should note that doubling to 1,300 downloads per episode in 12 months is achievable but requires systematic promotion.
expectations: Identifies LinkedIn as the primary rented channel for this audience
Recommends platform-native LinkedIn content (not just linking to the episode)
Recommends show notes as SEO-optimized blog posts
Includes guest appearances on other financial advisor shows as a tactic
Produces a post-publish promotion checklist with specific timing (day 0, day 3, etc.)
